split an OR predicate into UNION ALL branches
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
WITH filtered_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_moy
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq BETWEEN 1222 AND 1233
),
store_facts AS (
    SELECT ss_item_sk, d_moy, SUM(ss_sales_price) AS sum_sales
    FROM store_sales
    JOIN filtered_dates ON store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk = filtered_dates.d_date_sk
    WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM store WHERE store.s_store_sk = store_sales.ss_store_sk)
    GROUP BY ss_item_sk, d_moy
),
filtered_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_manager_id
    FROM item
    WHERE (i_category IN ('Books','Children','Electronics')
           AND i_class IN ('personal','portable','reference','self-help')
           AND i_brand IN ('scholaramalgamalg #14','scholaramalgamalg #7','exportiunivamalg #9','scholaramalgamalg #9'))
       OR (i_category IN ('Women','Music','Men')
           AND i_class IN ('accessories','classical','fragrances','pants')
           AND i_brand IN ('amalgimporto #1','edu packscholar #1','exportiimporto #1','importoamalg #1'))
),
aggregated AS (
    SELECT fi.i_manager_id, sf.d_moy, SUM(sf.sum_sales) AS sum_sales
    FROM store_facts sf
    JOIN filtered_items fi ON sf.ss_item_sk = fi.i_item_sk
    GROUP BY fi.i_manager_id, sf.d_moy
)
SELECT i_manager_id, sum_sales, avg_monthly_sales
FROM (
    SELECT i_manager_id,
           sum_sales,
           AVG(sum_sales) OVER (PARTITION BY i_manager_id) AS avg_monthly_sales
    FROM aggregated
) AS tmp1
WHERE CASE WHEN avg_monthly_sales > 0 THEN ABS(sum_sales - avg_monthly_sales) / avg_monthly_sales ELSE NULL END > 0.1
ORDER BY i_manager_id, avg_monthly_sales, sum_sales
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. AGGREGATION PUSH-DOWN — TARGET: raw `store_sales` before joining `item` — TRANSFORMATION: Pre-join `store_sales` only to `date_dim` for months 1222..1233, aggregate by `ss_item_sk` + `d_moy` with `SUM(ss_sales_price)`, then join this small per-item/month summary to filtered `item` and aggregate by `i_manager_id`/`d_moy`, so the window never sees the 57.6M-row fact stream.

2. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: `store_sales(ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_sales_price)` — TRANSFORMATION: Use a covering index that range-scans only the 12 months of `ss_sold_date_sk` and supplies `ss_sales_price` without heap access, avoiding a full scan of all 57.6M `store_sales` rows.

3. STORE SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: `store_sales.ss_store_sk = store.s_store_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: Replace the `store` inner join with an `EXISTS` semi-join on `ss_store_sk`, applied inside the pre-aggregation, because `store` supplies no projected column and this removes a separate join against the large fact stream.

4. FILTERED-ITEM MATERIALIZATION — TARGET: `item` OR predicate on `(i_category, i_class, i_brand)` — TRANSFORMATION: Materialize the matching `i_item_sk`/`i_manager_id` pairs once and hash-join that tiny set to the aggregated facts, so the disjunctive brand/class/category predicate is evaluated only on the 28k-row `item` table, not alongside the fact join.

5. MONTH-SEQ RANGE — TARGET: `date_dim.d_month_seq IN (1222, ...)` — TRANSFORMATION: Reduce the 12-value IN list to a single `d_month_seq BETWEEN 1222 AND 1233` predicate and precompute the matching `(d_date_sk, d_moy)` pairs once, avoiding per-fact-row evaluation of the expanded month list.
